IsValidEmail is also duplicated between ComposeEndpoints and Compose.razor rather than living in Feirb.Shared. A typo or rename in any one copy silently breaks Unprotect for that path (CryptographicException at send time). The two IsValidEmail copies can drift apart, so the client accepts addresses the server rejects.

The Task.Delay(50) and lazy-init branch in SwitchToRichTextAsync are dead in practice: Quill is always initialized in OnAfterRenderAsync, since RichText is the initial mode and the container is only hidden with display:none. Each Markdown→Rich switch adds an arbitrary 50ms delay plus a timing-dependent code path that never runs. If it ever did run, it would rely on a fixed delay instead of OnAfterRender.

postCreateCommand installs `.[dev]`, but pyproject.toml (hatchling backend, which ignores setup.py) has no `[project.optional-dependencies] dev`, so pytest, ruff, black and mypy never get installed. The container builds and uv prints a warning that the package has no extra named `dev`, then installs only the runtime deps. `pytest`/`mypy` are missing in the venv, so README step 2's claim that it 'installs all Python dependencies' is wrong. Fix: add a `dev` optional-dependencies table to pyproject.toml that mirrors requirements-dev.in, or install `-r requirements-dev.in`.

workspaceFolder is hardcoded to `/workspaces/ProxmoxMCP-Plus` without a matching `workspaceMount`, but the default mount target is `/workspaces/<local folder basename>`. Say a user clones into `proxmox-mcp`, a fork with a different name, or `ProxmoxMCP-Plus-main` from a zip. The repo gets mounted at `/workspaces/proxmox-mcp`, VS Code opens an empty or missing `/workspaces/ProxmoxMCP-Plus`, postCreateCommand runs where there's no pyproject.toml and fails, and the interpreter path points nowhere. Use `/workspaces/${localWorkspaceFolderBasename}` in both workspaceFolder and python.defaultInterpreterPath, or add an explicit workspaceMount.

python.defaultInterpreterPath hardcodes `/workspaces/ProxmoxMCP-Plus/.venv/bin/python`, so it breaks whenever the mount path differs from the repo name. With any other clone directory name, Pylance and the Python extension can't find the interpreter. Imports show as unresolved and tests can't be discovered even after the venv exists. Use `${containerWorkspaceFolder}/.venv/bin/python`.

`uv venv` runs inside the bind-mounted workspace, so it replaces any `.venv` the developer already built on the host (macOS/Windows) with a Linux venv. The reverse happens too: the container's venv breaks host tooling. A developer who followed the README's local install steps (`uv venv` at README.md:99) opens the repo in the container. postCreateCommand recreates `.venv` with Linux binaries, and their host `source .venv/bin/activate` / Claude Desktop config at `.venv/bin/python` stops working. Depending on the uv version, `uv venv` may also prompt or fail on an existing venv when the container is rebuilt. Point the venv outside the workspace with `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`/`VIRTUAL_ENV`, e.g. `/home/vscode/.venv`, or use a named volume for `.venv`.

The README says the OpenAPI proxy 'is reachable at http://localhost:8811', but the dev container never starts the proxy. Only the port is forwarded. A user follows steps 1–4, opens http://localhost:8811 and gets connection refused, because there's no postStartCommand. They have to know to run `./start_openapi.sh` themselves. Reword the step to tell them to run the proxy first, or add a postStartCommand.

`pip install --no-cache-dir uv` installs an unpinned uv, so `uv venv` / `uv pip` behavior can drift between rebuilds. A later uv release changes how `uv venv` handles an existing directory (newer releases have already moved toward requiring `--clear`). Rebuilding the container then fails or prompts in postCreateCommand with no change to the repo. Pin a uv version, or use the official `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv` image via `COPY --from`.

The build context is set to `..`, the whole repo, but the dev container Dockerfile has no COPY/ADD, and the repo has no .dockerignore. Every image build sends the full repo to the Docker daemon for nothing: `.git`, any local `.venv`, test artifacts, and `proxmox-config/config.json` with its secrets. That slows builds and can leak credentials into the build cache. Set `context` to `.` or drop it.

The Dockerfile rebuilds by hand what `mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.11` already gives you: a non-root `vscode` user with UID/GID handling, git, curl and build tools. That's about 20 lines of user/apt setup to maintain, and the hand-made user has no sudo, so a developer can't `apt-get install` anything inside the container. Using the devcontainers base image (plus the uv feature) would cut the custom Dockerfile down to almost nothing.

`WORKDIR /home/$USERNAME` is dead config: devcontainer.json's workspaceFolder decides where VS Code and postCreateCommand run. It has no effect, and it suggests the home directory is where the work happens. Remove it.

The new topics file has no matching `.github/workflows/deploy-aktivitetspenger-inntektsrapportering-topics.yml`, but every other topics file has one (e.g. deploy-aktivitetspenger-soknad-topics.yml, deploy-ungdomsytelse-inntektsrapportering-topics.yml). After merge, nothing applies the Topic resources in dev/prod. The three new streams, and the producer for `dusseldorf.aktivitetspenger-inntektsrapportering-mottatt`, point at topics that don't exist. Health indicators go DOWN and every submission fails, or is lost, once it reaches Kafka.

`@AssertTrue` sits on `fun harOppgittInntekt()`. Hibernate Validator only evaluates getter-style methods (get/is/has), so this constraint never runs and a null `arbeidstakerOgFrilansInntekt` passes validation. The same applies to `OppgittInntektForPeriode.harOppgittInntekt`. A POST with `{"oppgaveReferanse":"<uuid>","oppgittInntekt":{}}` returns 202 instead of 400. A k9 søknad with null inntekt is published, and the oppgave is marked solved with `RapportertInntektDto(..., null)`. No test covers this rule.

The k9 format for an income report is a plain `Aktivitetspenger` ytelse with `medSøknadsperiode(inntektsperiode)` and no søknadstype marker. The ungdomsytelse counterpart sets `UngSøknadstype.RAPPORTERING_SØKNAD`. ung-sak reads `aktivitetspenger-inntektsrapportering-cleanup` (ACL in the topics file). It gets a payload that looks like a new aktivitetspenger application whose søknadsperiode is the reported month. Downstream it can be handled as a new søknad or startdato rather than an income report.

`AKTIVITETSPENGER_INNTEKTRAPPORTERING` uses a placeholder brevkode `FIXME_AVP_INNTEKT_BREVKODE`, and that value is sent to dokarkiv on journalføring. Journalposts are created with an invalid brevkode. Either dokarkiv rejects them, so the journalføring stream retries and then fails, or they are archived with the wrong document classification in production.

`markerOppgaveSomLøst` is called only after `forsikreIkkeDuplikatInnsending` has recorded the key and `innsendingService.registrer` has published to Kafka. ung-brukerdialog-api times out or returns 5xx while marking the oppgave. The user gets an error, but the report is already on Kafka and will be journalført. When they retry, they get a duplicate-innsending rejection, and the oppgave stays ULØST.

The duplicate-check cache key is `personIdent_ytelse`, with no oppgaveReferanse, so all of a user's income reports share one key. A user with two open RAPPORTER_INNTEKT oppgaver (e.g. two months) submits both within the cache TTL. The second, legitimate report is rejected as a duplicate.

The income report is validated with `AktivitetspengerSøknadValidator`, the validator for the full application. The report only sets søknadsperiode and inntekter, with no forutgåendeBosteder. If the validator enforces application-only fields (bosteder or other søknad requirements), every income report fails k9-format validation during `innsendingService.registrer` and returns 400. I couldn't check this: the k9-format 12.10.0 jar isn't cached locally.

The new controller test imports `no.nav.brukerdialog.ytelse.ungdomsytelse.utils.InntektrapporteringUtils` instead of the new `ytelse.aktivitetspenger.utils.InntektrapporteringUtils`. It also stubs an unused `barnService.hentBarn()`. The test sends an ungdomsytelse request object to the aktivitetspenger endpoint. If the aktivitetspenger request type drifts (new required field, different validation), this test keeps passing while real clients break.

`OppgittInntekt`, `OppgittInntektForPeriode`, `UngPeriode`, the PdfData class, the .hbs template and `hentInntektsrapporteringPeriode` are near-verbatim copies of the ungdomsytelse inntektsrapportering versions. There are now two copies of the same domain/PDF/validation logic. The inert `@AssertTrue` above already exists in both, and fixes must be made twice. Move the shared types to a common package (e.g. `fellesdomene`) and reuse them from both ytelser.

The cleanup topic bean is named `aktivitetpengerInntektsrapporteringCleanupTopic` (missing 's'), while both consumers inject a parameter named `aktivitetspengerInntektsrapporteringCleanupTopic`. Wiring works only through generic-type matching. If another bean with a compatible `Topic<...>` type is added, Spring falls back to matching by name, finds no bean named `aktivitetspengerInntektsrapporteringCleanupTopic`, and startup fails with NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException.

The "*" (keep) case only looks up existingCred.Env[u] under the new URL key, but the UI's rename flow moves "*" from oldUrl to the new URL, so the stored token is never carried over despite the comment claiming it is. Admin edits source https://github.com/org/private to https://github.com/org/private/dev. The UI sends sourceURLCredentials{"…/dev":"*"}. existingCred.Env has no "…/dev" key, so newTokens is empty and the credential is deleted. The next sync fails with an auth error and the PAT is gone.

Scheme-less SourceURLs get rewritten to https://…, but the keys in SourceURLCredentials are left as typed, so they never match activeURLs and the submitted token is thrown away. User adds source "gitlab.com/org/repo" with a PAT. SourceURLs becomes "https://gitlab.com/org/repo" while the credential key stays "gitlab.com/org/repo". That key is skipped as inactive, the token is never stored, and the request still returns success.

isGitRepoURL now treats every gitlab.com URL as a git repo, so raw-file URLs on gitlab.com that used to be fetched over HTTP now go through parseGitURL and fail. An existing source https://gitlab.com/org/repo/-/raw/main/catalog.yaml used to work as a raw file. Now parseGitURL reads the branch as "-/raw/main/catalog.yaml". validateBranchName rejects it because it starts with "-", so every sync of that source fails.

The old code sent GITHUB_AUTH_TOKEN for every github.com catalog clone and API size check. It is now only used when the URL exactly equals the hard-coded default catalog URL, and existing configs are not migrated. After upgrade, a deployment that relied on GITHUB_AUTH_TOKEN for a private GitHub catalog (or for rate limiting) starts failing clones with auth or 403/rate-limit errors until an admin adds a per-URL token. URL variants of the default catalog (trailing slash, /main branch suffix, .git) also lose the fallback.

The catalog spec is saved before the credential is created or deleted, so a credential-store failure leaves new URLs saved without their tokens, and a sync can run between the two writes without the token. CreateCredential fails because the credential store is briefly unavailable. The API returns 500, but catalog.Spec.SourceURLs already holds the new private URL. Its token is never stored, the next sync records an auth error, and the user may assume the save didn't happen.

sizeLimitedFS wraps both the .git storage and the worktree, so pack bytes and checked-out file bytes add up against one 100 MB budget. That is far stricter than the API pre-check, which only looks at packed repo size. A repo with a 55 MB pack and about 60 MB checkout passes the GitHub API size check (55 MB < 100 MB). The clone then fails with "repository is too large" once the combined writes pass 100 MB, so a valid catalog can never sync.

revealCatalogCredential fetches the same catalog-wide credential on every iteration of the source URL loop. Any non-not-found error is only logged, not added to SyncErrors as its doc comment says. A catalog with N sources does N identical credential-store reveals per sync. If the store errors, every private source fails with a misleading auth/clone error in SyncErrors and the real cause only appears in server logs. Revealing once before the loop and recording the error per URL fixes both.

List and Get now decrypt the full secret token map for every catalog just to output "*" markers, and any credential-store error fails the whole List or Get request. A transient credential-store error makes GET /mcp-catalogs return 500, so the catalog UI breaks even for users who never touch tokens. Each List also does one secret reveal per catalog; ListCredentials (no reveal) or tolerating errors would avoid both problems.

The "*" switch case and the separate "preserve unmentioned URLs" loop do the same thing (copy existingCred.Env[u]). Two code paths now encode the keep-existing rule, and the comment on the "*" path ("transferred from a renamed one") already disagrees with what the code does. A single loop over manifest.SourceURLs that only overrides on "" or a new value would be simpler and keep that rule in one place.

readGitCatalog parses the URL again and rebuilds repoPath by trimming prefixes off cloneURL, even though parseGitURL already computed repoPath. readGitCatalog's doc comment also got merged into parseGitURL's comment block at line 212. The trimming logic duplicates parseGitURL's job and can drift from it, e.g. if cloneURL formatting changes. Returning repoPath from parseGitURL removes the second url.Parse and the string surgery. The misplaced comment leaves readGitCatalog undocumented and parseGitURL's doc contradictory.

parseGitHubUrl matches the branch segment of /tree/<branch>/ but throws it away, so resolveIdentifier always fetches from the repo's default branch. `spm install https://github.com/org/repo/tree/develop/path/to/skill` fetches skillset.yml from `main`. It either 404s or installs the wrong version. The test 'parses GitHub URL with non-main branch' only checks owner, repo and path, so it never catches this.

safePath uses `resolved.startsWith(baseDir)` with no path separator, so sibling directories that share the prefix get through the traversal check. baseDir is `/tmp/spm/fsd` and a manifest entry resolves to `/tmp/spm/fsd-evil/x`. `startsWith` returns true and the file is written outside the intended directory. Check `resolved === baseDir || resolved.startsWith(baseDir + sep)` instead.

tmpDir is built from `skillset.name`, which comes straight from the remote manifest with no checks, so the base directory used by safePath can itself point anywhere. A manifest with `name: ../../../home/user/.ssh` makes `join(tmpdir(),'spm',name)` resolve outside tmp. safePath then compares against that already-escaped base, so every file write lands in an attacker-chosen directory.

The '..' traversal check only covers bare-path sources. `./` sources, `@` sources and each `files` entry are joined into paths with no check, and the substring test also rejects legitimate names like `foo..bar`. `source: './../../../other-owner/other-repo/main'` or `files: ['../../x']` passes through. Fetch normalizes the dot segments, so the raw.githubusercontent.com URL can pull files from a different repo. Meanwhile `source: 'skills..v2'` is wrongly rejected. Validate once per path segment (segment === '..') over the final path of every entry.

The old 'Invalid skill source' error was replaced by a catch-all bare-path fallback, so any malformed source is now silently treated as a repo-root path. A typo like `.claude/skill` (meant `./claude/skill`), an empty string, or `https://example.com/x` is no longer rejected. Downloads then 404 against a path like `https://example.com/x/SKILL.md`, or `''` becomes `/SKILL.md`, and the error message no longer explains the cause.

The regex treats the first segment after /tree/ as the whole branch name, so branches that contain slashes are split wrongly. For `https://github.com/org/repo/tree/feature/new-skill/claude/fsd`, the branch is parsed as `feature` and the path as `new-skill/claude/fsd`, so the wrong skillset.yml path is fetched. A trailing slash or a `?query`/`#hash` also ends up in the path.

The download dir `/tmp/spm/<name>` is predictable, shared, never cleaned and never made unique, so stale files build up and other local users can plant symlinks in it. Reinstalling a skillset after a file was removed upstream leaves the old file in tmpDir, and it gets reported and used. On a multi-user Linux host, another user can pre-create `/tmp/spm/fsd/...` as a symlink, and writeFile follows it. Use mkdtemp, or rm the directory before writing.

A generated project config (`.spmrc.yml`) was committed to the repo root. It looks like a side effect of running the CLI or integration tests, because readConfig() auto-creates it. The repo now ships a machine-specific provider detection result, and running the integration tests (`install`, which calls readConfig) keeps writing into the real repo root instead of a temp directory.

Every download is decoded with `response.text()` and written back as utf-8, which corrupts any non-text file a skill includes. A skill that ships an image, a zip or another binary asset gets invalid byte sequences replaced with U+FFFD, and the installed file is silently broken. Use `arrayBuffer()` and write a Buffer.

downloadFromGitHub rebuilds the same raw.githubusercontent.com URL-and-fetch logic that fetchSkillset already has, and resolveSkillSource's `@` parsing duplicates parseAtIdentifier. There are two copies of the URL building, error formatting and @owner/repo/path parsing. A fix to one (auth headers, ref encoding, validation) can easily miss the other. fetchSkillset should call downloadFromGitHub, and resolveSkillSource should reuse parseAtIdentifier.

The raw Deployment drops the chart's `envFrom: secretRef: ms-secret-vault`, so the agent no longer receives the Vault-synced secrets, such as the MySQL password. backend/ai-secure-agent-config.yaml configures MySQL as `username: root` with no password, and Kafka/Redis credentials also come from the ExternalSecret `ms-secret-vault` (k8s-configs/eos-microservice.yaml). The chart injected that secret through envFrom (charts/templates/deployment.yaml:76-78). Without it, the pod starts with no DB, Kafka or LLM secrets, so MySQL auth fails and the service crash-loops or returns errors.

agent-app is pinned to the feature branch `AI-20-AISecureAgent-Feature-collection`, while every other app tracks HEAD. Argo syncs `agent/` from the feature branch, not from main. Changes merged to main's agent/ai-secure-agent.yaml (tag bumps, the secret fix) never deploy. If that branch is deleted after merge, or lacks the `agent/` dir, the app goes ComparisonError/Unknown. With `prune: true`, an empty or missing path can prune the running Deployment.

Deleting the values dir makes the helm-app ApplicationSet delete its generated `ai-secure-agent-ms` Application, which cascade-deletes a Deployment and Service with the same names agent-app now creates. Both apps manage `Deployment/ai-secure-agent-ms` and `Service/ai-secure-agent-ms-svc` in `default`. The ApplicationSet-generated Application carries the resources finalizer, so removing it deletes those objects. Depending on sync order, agent-app's freshly applied Deployment and Service get deleted (outage until selfHeal re-creates them), or Argo flags a SharedResource conflict while both apps exist.

The image tag is now hardcoded in a raw manifest, but the CI tag-bump flow writes `image.tag` into `helm_backend/<svc>/values.yaml`. History shows CI bot commits editing helm_backend/ai-secure-agent-ms/values.yaml (e.g. cffc861). The next CI bump either fails or re-creates helm_backend/ai-secure-agent-ms/values.yaml with only `image.tag`. That spawns a new helm-app Application that renders broken (missing probes, volumes and resources) and fights agent-app over the same resource names. The agent image itself never gets bumped.

CPU and memory requests and limits were dropped. The old values (256Mi request, 345Mi limit) had been tuned for this service. The pod now runs BestEffort with no memory cap on a shared single-node k3s cluster. An LLM or MLflow memory spike can OOM neighbouring services, and BestEffort pods are evicted first under node pressure. MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 was set alongside the 345Mi limit, which suggests memory growth was a known issue.

Liveness and readiness probes on `/ai-secure-agent-ms/v1/ping` were dropped. The Service routes traffic to the pod as soon as the container starts, before config, MySQL and Kafka are ready. A hung Python process (e.g. a deadlocked Kafka consumer) is never restarted. The chart enforced both probes for every backend service.

The `applogs` hostPath volume (/tmp/logs/ai-secure-agent-ms mounted at /app/logs) and its fix-perm initContainer were dropped. If the app writes to /app/logs, as every chart-based service does, the logs now go to the container's ephemeral filesystem. They are lost on restart and missing from the host path that other services' logs use. If the image's runtime user can't create /app/logs, file logging fails.

The shared Helm chart is hand-copied into a raw manifest only to deploy this service from a different branch, which duplicates the chart and loses its invariants. Every chart behaviour (secret injection, probes, resources, anti-affinity, log volume, HPA) now has to be re-added and maintained by hand for one service, and it has already drifted (findings above). A cleaner fix: keep helm_backend/ai-secure-agent-ms/values.yaml and use a separate Application for the `charts` path with this values file, if a separate revision is truly needed.

resolveURL prefers status.endpoints.admin/public, which the operator always sets to http://{name}-keycloak.{ns}.svc.cluster.local:8080, so the CLI (run outside the cluster) always gets an unreachable URL; the spec.hostname fallback is dead because KeycloakSpec has no `hostname` field (it is spec.ingress.host / spec.tls.hostname). User runs the documented `import-users --keycloak my-keycloak --namespace keycloak-system --realm my-realm` from a laptop: target resolves to http://my-keycloak-keycloak.keycloak-system.svc.cluster.local:8080 and the token request fails with a DNS error. The default cluster-mode path never works without --server-url.

decodeSecretKey base64-decodes any value that happens to look like base64 (length%4==0, alphanumeric), even though client-go already returns decoded bytes, so plain usernames and passwords get turned into garbage. The operator generates 16-char passwords from letters+digits+`!@#$%^&*`; about 14% are purely alphanumeric and decode "successfully" to random bytes, so auth fails with 401. Usernames like `test` or `root` and passwords like `Password1234` break the same way.

Keycloak's PartialImportResults JSON has `added`, `skipped`, `overwritten`, `results` and `errorMessage`, but no `errors` field, and result actions are only ADDED/SKIPPED/OVERWRITTEN. So Errors is always 0, the `errors > 0` hard-fail and ERROR/FAILED detail collection never run, and overwritten counts are thrown away. An OVERWRITE run over 5000 existing users prints `Added: 0, Skipped: 0, Errors: 0`, which looks like nothing happened. The ADR's promised errors>0 failure detection never triggers; real failures only show up as non-200 HTTP codes.

On token-refresh, HTTP 403/409/5xx or parse failures, ImportUsers returns `nil, err` and drops the totals collected so far, so the caller's "print partial result before returning error" prints nothing. In FAIL mode, batch 7/10 gets a 409. The user sees only the error and no count of the 3000 users already imported by batches 1-6, which is exactly the progress info the cmd comment promises.

authenticate and importBatch use http.DefaultClient (no timeout), and the command passes context.Background() with no signal handling, so a stalled Keycloak or proxy hangs the import forever. A 500-user batch with credential hashes hits an ingress that accepts the connection but never answers. The CLI hangs with no timeout and no clean cancellation, so CI jobs sit until their global timeout.

The 409 branch always says `mode=FAIL`, but Keycloak can return 409 in SKIP/OVERWRITE mode too (e.g. duplicate email or another unique-constraint clash inside the batch). A SKIP-mode run fails with "HTTP 409 Conflict (mode=FAIL)". The operator then hunts for a misconfigured --mode flag instead of the duplicate-email data problem.

The importer writes dry-run and per-batch progress to stdout with fmt.Printf, while the command writes loading/summary lines with cobra's cmd.Printf (stderr by default), so output is split across streams and can't be captured or redirected together. `import-users --dry-run > plan.txt` puts the dry-run plan in plan.txt while the Loaded/Resolved/summary lines go to the terminal. In CI logs the two streams interleave out of order.

The only explicit-credential path is `--password`, which docs recommend for CI. The admin password then shows up in process listings and shell history; there is no env-var or stdin option. In a CI runner or shared bastion, `ps aux` or /proc/<pid>/cmdline exposes the Keycloak master-realm admin password for the whole multi-batch import.

currentKubeNamespace builds the same NonInteractiveDeferredLoadingClientConfig that ResolveFromCluster builds again. Namespace defaulting could live in ResolveFromCluster and use the same ClientConfig's Namespace(). Kubeconfig is loaded and parsed twice per run, and the two copies can drift (e.g. adding a --context/--kubeconfig override to one but not the other would resolve the namespace from a different cluster than the CR).

LoadUsersFile unmarshals the whole file into json.RawMessage (a full validation scan) just to check the first byte, then unmarshals it again into []map[string]any. Unmarshalling straight into the slice already rejects objects and scalars. For a 50k-user export with credential hashes (hundreds of MB), parse work doubles for no gain. Trimming leading whitespace and checking for `[`, or just relying on the typed-unmarshal error, does the same job in one pass.
